title: Teddy Wilson and Fletcher Henderson
summary: Fletcher Henderson's wife copied for Benny; Sauter's respect for Fletcher; Fletcher's band early in the evening.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Teddy Wilson; wonderful, a lovely human being. And Fletcher, a very kind human being. Fletcher's wife I used to--Fletcher's wife used to copy from Benny and I'd run things down there at three thirty, four o'clock in the morning and never a problem.
She lived on 138th Street and Lenox Avenue somewhere. Don't go there alone now, especially if you're white. But in those days they didn't do anything.
Horace Henderson in his oral history interview said that Benny used to call Fletcher in the middle of the night and tell him, will you please do such and such a chart, I need it for a recording
session the next day, or something like that. Did you know about any of that, or did that happen to you?
No. He would say something if I somehow sometimes didn't get the two or three a week in. That happened occasionally, but no, he would always take from that.
Did you know Fletcher very well?

How well? I don't know how to answer. I knew him as one would know a co-worker, a close co-worker, which was pretty good. There was always respect and he was always very kind. He was the elder statesman at that point. Benny had built his band around Fletcher's arrangements and I was suppose to imitate that, I think, but I never really could. Maybe Fletcher respected me because I didn't; I don't know.
I imagine he did. Did you get to hear Fletcher's band in its heyday?
Yes, and it sounded awful. Maybe because I heard them always early in the evening. They were down on the Post Road at a place I was working.
This was late twenties, early thirties?
Yes. It was always rather slipshod, but always very much personality involved. I've forgotten who the players were, but that could easily be found out.
Coleman Hawkins probably. He was there until about '34.
